task:
Galaxy map nebulae: cloud appearance and landmark persistence (review finding M03). apps/web only. Keep the M02 inventory/count contract exactly as merged (galaxy-nebulae-policy.ts counts, receipts, status line).

VERIFIED ON MAIN:
- `apps/web/src/lib/spatial/babylon/adapter.ts` `createGalaxyNebulaeMesh()` renders every diffuse landmark as a thin-instanced 16-segment sphere (StandardMaterial, backFaceCulling off, alpha 0.45, vertex colour alpha 0.4-0.65, no texture), flattened to 0.62 on Y, radius `nebulaCloudRadiusLy() * (0.65 + hash*1.25)`; colour from `NEBULA_PALETTE[regionId or hash]`. At regional zoom these read as overlapping dark-edged coloured discs, not clouds.
- `galaxy-nebulae-policy.ts`: the whole diffuse layer fades from NEBULA_LANDMARK_FADE_START_LY 8,000 to NEBULA_LANDMARK_FADE_END_LY 2,000 and is hidden below 2,000 LY, so a nebula disappears as the commander approaches it. Planetary nebulae are small markers (PLANETARY_NEBULA_MARKER_RADIUS_LY 3) with their own fade.
- The catalogue (`/assets/edastro-mapcharts-nebulae.json`) carries positions only; it has no measured extents. Current radii are decorative.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Separate the two concerns per diffuse nebula: a NAVIGABLE LANDMARK (small stable marker at the catalogue position; never hidden by the cloud fade; keeps the existing hover/name behaviour if any, otherwise no new picking) and a DECORATIVE CLOUD.
2. Render the cloud as soft, irregular, depth-aware translucent billboards instead of opaque-edged spheres: 2-3 camera-facing (or crossed) quads per landmark with a small procedurally generated alpha texture atlas (soft radial falloff plus low-frequency noise; generate at startup into a DynamicTexture or RawTexture; no new runtime dependencies, no binary assets, no external fetches). Additive or premultiplied blending without depth write so overlaps brighten rather than darken; disable picking. Stable variation per landmark from the existing identity hash (rotation, which atlas tile, slight colour shift). Keep the palette family; reduce per-cloud alpha so dense regions do not wash out stars.
3. Honest extents: keep radii schematic but bound them (document the chosen range in a policy constant with a comment that no authorised source supplies extents) and expose that in the layer metadata/legend text (`nebulaDisplayStatus` / Layers pop-out) as "schematic extent" wording. Do not invent measured sizes.
4. Approach behaviour: the cloud may fade with distance so the camera is never inside an opaque blob, but the landmark marker must remain visible at every zoom level where catalogue stars are shown, so a nebula is still findable at close range. Use distinct enter/exit thresholds (hysteresis) so the cloud does not flicker at the boundary. Receipts/counts: `renderedTargetCount` and visible counts must reflect markers and clouds truthfully (document which is counted).
5. Performance: one draw call per atlas/material for all clouds (thin instances on a plane mesh) and one for markers; no per-frame allocations; keep the existing dispose paths. Must still run under the SwiftShader/ANGLE headless lane.
6. Tests: unit tests for the texture atlas generator (deterministic, bounded size), the hysteresis visibility function, the bounded schematic radius, and adapter tests that the marker mesh persists below 2,000 LY while the cloud mesh fades; update `nebula-adapter.test.ts` and policy tests accordingly. Keep every existing nebula count assertion passing.
7. Append a CHANGES.md entry at the top. Visual validation (Product E2E screenshots) is required before any production promotion; say so in the entry and do not deploy.

Non-goals: no change to the planetary-nebula class beyond keeping it working; no raymarched volumes; no new assets or dependencies; no backend change; no Layers pop-out structure change beyond legend wording.
